description: Draft contracts this build can read ONLY through the explicitly requested rule-V7 lane. These are not released contracts: neither type has a row in the shared schemas/versions.json, a published schemaVersion of its own, a w3id URL or a release tag, and nothing in this file changes that. Each entry pins the exact bytes of one draft file by the commit of the development repository that owns the type and the SHA-256 of those bytes, which is how docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md V7 requires a draft to be read: selection runs against the pinned bytes, never against a repository's main at run time. Two revisions are pinned per type and they are different things: `commit` is the revision of the contract bytes this library compiles and validates against, and `suiteCommit` is the revision of the owning repository's development conformance suite whose manifest `scripts/capability/draft-vectors.mjs` executes. They are separate keys because the two files move at different times, and because the suite carries the rule labels this file quotes: a claim about C1/C2/C3 is a claim about the suite revision, never about the contract revision. Where they are equal, `suiteCommit` repeats `commit` so the check is uniform. `src/drafts.js` re-verifies every digest the first time a draft is loaded and refuses to read on a mismatch. The lane is never the default: with no explicit user decision these files are not read at all and a draft citation is 'any other value' under V5, exactly as it was before the lane existed. This registry is deliberately separate from schemas/provenance.json, which lists released contracts only and stays that way.
rule: docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md rule V7 (FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification#221/#226, text published at tag v0.6.0)

scheduledPublication.note: A scheduled future release is a decision about that type, not a licence to publish it here. Until the release lands these entries stay drafts: no schemaVersion claim, no fixed alias, no registry row, no support claim.

retrieved: 2026-11-14 (contract bytes), re-measured 2026-11-16T04:20Z (that pass moved the two suites and neither contract), re-pinned 2026-11-18T21:45Z for the coordinated round-13 draft re-pin. **This re-pin moves BOTH contract byte sets** - the first time contract bytes have moved under this lane - together with both suite manifests and the FHGM transport overlay. The 2026-11-16 note's assurance that the contract bytes did not move was true of the revision it recorded and is false of this one; it has been rewritten here rather than left in place as a stale claim.
retrievalMethod: Every digest recorded here was computed from bytes actually downloaded, never from a HEAD content-length and never from raw.githubusercontent.com at a moving branch name. 2026-11-18 pass: both owning repositories were cloned fresh over HTTPS (FHT-Specification origin/main at 0311ddacbf7559d4160054d23db6fd06898f45a9, FHGM-Specification origin/main at b1a82f82f8a2d4a5f5e78240edaa05c6bd9222d8), each target was read out of the Git object database at the pinned commit with `git show <commit>:<path>` and hashed with `shasum -a 256`, each pinned commit was confirmed an ancestor of that head with no later commit touching the same path, and every file was `cmp`-ed byte-equal against the same path at origin/main. The git blob ids are recorded in each `verification` so the pin, the head and the downloaded bytes can be re-anchored without re-downloading anything. Earlier passes used the GitHub contents API at ref=main with the API blob sha recomputed from the downloaded bytes; the 2026-11-16 observation that the raw-main CDN served pre-merge bytes for minutes after a merge is why no measurement here is taken from that CDN at a branch name. The raw-main URLs in `citation` are what a reader cites and what the advisory freshness check probes; they are not how these numbers were measured.

FHT.suiteCommitNote: This re-pin **moves the FHT contract bytes**, and it says so plainly because the note it replaces asserted the opposite: the 2026-11-16 revision said 'this re-pin moves no contract byte', which was true of that suite-only move and is false of this one, so it is rewritten rather than left to rot. `MoleculeType` grew from four values to five - `mixed` added, which the new bytes define as explicitly recording known heterogeneous RNA classes, not uncertainty - `properties.schema` became a const admitting only the raw-main citation (the release-tag and w3id URL forms the old pattern allowed are now rejected by the contract itself while FHT is an unreleased draft, and the suite's new `fht-fasta-schema-shared-raw-tag` vector pins that), and the remaining patterns were made dialect-portable (FHT-Specification#54). Contract and suite had to move together, and they did. This was demonstrated in a scratch build, not reasoned about: the OLD contract bytes against the NEW 82-vector suite scored 80 pass, 2 fail - `fht-fasta-molecule-type-mixed` (expected valid) is rejected by the four-value old enum, and `fht-fasta-blank-version-separator` (expected invalid) is accepted by the old non-portable pattern and rejected only by the dialect-portable one - so a suite-only re-pin is arithmetically impossible, and a contract-only one would strand ten vectors. (The round-13 audit predicted five accept->reject flips at contract level; this build measured exactly these two, and records what it measured.) Both FHT revisions are now the same commit, `86438f21c3a17a58334c97aed4955be1a2393522`: it is the commit that last touched `conformance/manifest.json`, it also last touched `fht.json`, and no commit between it and the measured head 0311dda touches either file. That is the convention this repository adopted for all five pinned targets in this re-pin - each pin names the owning repository's last-touched-the-suite-manifest commit, and byte identity of every pinned artifact at that commit and at the live head is proven by git blob id before anything is recorded - which also settles the four-libraries-recorded-different-commits-for-identical-bytes divergence round 13 found; no digest changed because a commit label moved.

FHT.note: An FHT header is a FASTA `;~` block like FHR, so it shares the FASTA container; the type is decided by the record's own `schema` citation. Its conformance rules are C1 (contract validation), C2 (schema-URL closure) and C3 (parent-link verification) - text in the FHT-Specification conformance README. C2 is inside the pinned bytes; C3 is implemented here in src/parent-links.js.

FHGM.suiteCommitNote: This re-pin **moves the FHGM record-contract bytes too** - `bf1553ca...`/9,564 B is superseded by `b7075e58...`/11,522 B - so the note it replaces ('the record contract stayed at its own pin while the suite moved', true on 2026-11-16) is rewritten, not left standing. All three FHGM targets are pinned at 06176262f9824f26d974a15d8feeebde1fbeb0a8, the commit that last touched `development/conformance/manifest.json`, under the one-convention rule this repository adopted for all five targets this round; the record contract was also last touched there, and the transport overlay's own last-touched commit is 019bc29e32ce225791053dd2ce323bb91f304ce1 (FHGM-Specification#26) with byte-identical content at both revisions and at the measured head - git blob f7715d369a7e6f501f45416cc7417b1cffc5d4ea at all three, checked with `git rev-parse`, no digest changed. Two semantic notes about these bytes that NO digest diff and NO vector count detects, and that this pin therefore records in words. First: FHGM-Specification#29 widened what a `layers.model` **pass** means. Under the pinned bytes a pass now additionally implies text trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace and free of invisible/control characters ($defs/text), link URIs whose scheme is one FORMAT.md R14 accepts **with a real host** - javascript:, data:, vbscript: and file: are rejected outright ($defs/link) - non-blank deposits, identifier uniqueness compared after Unicode NFC, and a featureId that resolves to one ROOT gene row (no Parent). Upstream's README still calls the layers 'orthogonal'; that claim is an open question for the owning repository's maintainers, and no document in this repository restates it. Second: K4 still cannot abstain. FAIR-bioHeaders-Tools-JavaScript#11 records that a feature layer with no usable rows produces a `reject` where an abstention is what the disagreement with gff3-validator is about, and this library reaches K4 natively - so pinning the 62-vector suite means running a lane whose K4 abstention semantics are disputed upstream. The pin states that; it does not imply the draft suite is settled.

transportOverlay.note: Transport-only overlay. The bytes moved in this re-pin: `d1619cce...`/2,613 B is superseded by `533b3120...`/3,191 B. It no longer pins one FHGFF3 file identity: FHGM-Specification#17 (maintainer dual-base decision of 2026-11-15) rewrote it as a closed `anyOf` of two branch pairings, and FHGM-Specification#26 (019bc29e, the overlay's own last-touched commit; byte-identical at the pinned 06176262) widened the v0.6.0 branch: the pairing is now the v0.5.0 citation set with `schemaVersion` '1.1', or the v0.6.0 citation set with '1.2' **or '1.1'** - the v0.6.0 release accepts 1.1 records per the shared docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md - and the v0.6.0 URI set gained the raw tag URL under the FHR-Specification historical repository name, which the shared release recognises. A citation and a stated version that contradict each other (a v0.5.0 citation stating 1.2) stay rejected, and neither branch falls back to the other; `test/fhgm.test.mjs` covers the three admitted pairings, the contradiction and the inadmissible 1.0. FHGM carriers may now cite a release-tag URL of the *released* FHGFF3 contract - that is the carrier's own file identity under V2/V3, a released contract, and not a release form of the unreleased FHGM draft; the `fhr-specification-alias-v0.6.0` and `v0.6.0-citation-stating-1.1` vectors pin exactly that reading (rule V7 is about the draft's own citation, which stays raw-main-only). The overlay says nothing about record contents: those are the model contract above. It still requires a non-empty `x-fhgm-models` array of objects. This changes a documented divergence rather than recording a new number: `docs/CAPABILITY.md` and `src/fhgm.js` answered the pairing question for the two-branch overlay, and the pinned bytes now answer it for three pairings, which is why those rows and `test/fhgm.test.mjs` moved with this re-pin instead of being left to rot.

FHGM.note: FHGM is not a file header type: an FHGM record carries no `schema`, no `schemaVersion` and no `checksum`. Records ride inside an FHGFF3 header under the R15 extension key `x-fhgm-models`, the file keeps its released FHGFF3 citation and is routed by V1 to V3, and the file checksum covers every record byte (R3). The V7 lane therefore selects only the contract applied to the records. Model-level rules K1-K6 and the boundary B1 are drafted in FHGM-Specification; src/fhgm.js implements B1 and K1-K6, including K4 feature-target resolution against a feature layer - by default the enclosing file's own rows indexed for `type` and `ID` by src/features.js, or a resolver the caller injects - while full GFF3 feature validation remains with gff3-validator. A reading without a usable layer reports K4 `not-checked` or `unchecked`, never a pass and never a rejection. This sentence describes the consumer's implementation state and is not part of the pinned upstream bytes.
